main_body: A gnarled dark-brown tree trunk/root mass with a few small green moss patches, drawn on a stone-tile background in a 16x16 tile; no canopy visible
top_band: none - the trunk is brown from the top row downward with no lighter horizontal surface band; the top just fades into a branching silhouette
evidence: Reading a column through the middle (x~8-10): rows 0-2 are dark brown trunk, then continuous brown bark and root tones down to row 15. There is no lighter horizontal top surface, no front-edge line and no eave shadow. It is a flat front view of a trunk and roots, so it fails the 3/4 contract.

style.evidence: The candidate is a tiny brown trunk/root fragment with about 3 brown steps and a few dark green moss dabs. It has no leaf canopy, no clumps or highlights, and large areas of near-flat brown. Beside the references, which have 5-6 greens per canopy, tile-by-tile leaf texture and a dark-green or brown tinted outline, it is much thinner and flatter. The darkest outline pixels lean neutral/dark in places, so it reads as sticker-like.
